name: Burning Midnight Oil
description: One day a highly important task was commissioned to Vasya — writing a program in a night. The program consists of n lines of code. Vasya is already exhausted, so he works like that: first he writes v lines of code, drinks a cup of tea, then he writes as much as lines, drinks another cup of tea, then he writes lines and so on: , , , ... The expression is regarded as the integral part from dividing number a by number b . The moment the current value equals 0, Vasya immediately falls asleep and he wakes up only in the morning, when the program should already be finished. Vasya is wondering, what minimum allowable value v can take to let him write not less than n lines of code before he falls asleep.
input_specification: The input consists of two integers n and k , separated by spaces — the size of the program in lines and the productivity reduction coefficient, 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 9 , 2 ≤ k ≤ 10 .
output_specification: Print the only integer — the minimum value of v that lets Vasya write the program in one night.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 165B — Burning Midnight Oil [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
